The remaining proof obligations become two clean questions—does the product have enough gain, and can most of that gain be retained on at most N integers?

The weighted GCD form is bounded below by a normalized divisor sum A_N; multiplicativity factorizes A_N into local prime factors. Lemma 1 supplies the target lower bound for A_N, while Lemma 2 asks for a divisor-closed set M of cardinality at most N whose omitted normalized contribution is negligible.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Taking logarithms reveals that the Euler product is an accumulator: individually small prime contributions add, and prime density converts their total into the target iterated-logarithm scale. The chosen weight is tuned so that this integral lands at coefficient γ.

A prime-number-theorem approximation replaces this prime sum by an integral over the prime band, and changes of variables evaluate it as (γ+o(1)) times the required square-root iterated-logarithm expression, proving Lemma 1.
directed.conceptual_reading: Logarithmic linearization converts multiplicative amplification into additive bookkeeping. The prime-density integral is the macroscopic representation of many local gains and shows why the support band and singular-looking denominator in f(p) were chosen together.

directed.boundary_or_failure: This calculation proves the size of the unrestricted multiplicative functional A_N; it does not show that an N-element divisor-closed subset retains that size. That separate compression burden is Lemma 2.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the transformation chain and resulting scale. Broken square roots, integration limits, and iterated logarithms make exact constants and endpoints PDF-dependent.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The support is compressed by an occupancy budget rather than a size cutoff. Prime-number-theorem bounds for |P_k| together with factorial and binomial estimates yield |M|≤N when the parameters satisfy aγ<1.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The resonator is shortened in frequency space rather than arithmetic space. Since the zeta moment detects log(m/n), logarithmically nearby integers are interchangeable at the relevant resolution; clustering them and aggregating their squared weights preserves useful ratio mass while keeping the representative polynomial within the cardinality budget.

A Gaussian is chosen with positive, rapidly decaying Fourier transform. Starting from the divisor-closed set M with N=[T^κ], the integers are placed into multiplicative intervals of relative width about T^{-1}; one representative from each occupied interval forms M′, and its coefficient is the square root of the nearby f(n)^2 mass. Thus |M′|≤N.

The cluster coefficients then absorb those coincidences, and the surviving divisor pairs reconstruct the same A_N that powered the GCD theorem.

Lemmas 2 and 3 replace the restricted sum by A_N, Lemma 1 supplies its size, and division by the M1 bound yields Theorem 1.
